name: Woodrow H. Levin
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Extend (product-protection / extended-warranty platform for merchants)
profile: Serial founder Woody Levin co-founded Extend, a San Francisco platform that lets merchants sell product-protection plans online; it raised a $260M SoftBank-led Series C in 2021 at a $1.6B+ valuation. Earlier he founded gaming company BringIt (sold to IGT in 2012), stadium-ad firm InStadium and Estate Assist.
interesting_fact: He pitched Extend directly to SoftBank's Masayoshi Son, who he said 'immediately understood what we were doing'; his stated goal is to be the 'AppleCare' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
deep_cut_fact: Before Extend he founded InStadium, the NFL advertising company behind the ads in stadium bathrooms ('his idea'), and started Estate Assist (digital-asset estate planning) after watching his family of lawyers scramble for his grandmother's information after she died.

public_contacts.value: Danielle Vaknin, ASTRSK PR - extend@astrskpr.com (Extend media contact, Jan 2022 release)

notes: PR contact is from a 2022 release and may be stale. Search results also say he sits on the DraftKings board, but I could not open the DraftKings IR page to confirm it.

name: Aaron King
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Snapdocs (CEO until Sept 2023)
profile: Aaron King founded Snapdocs in 2013. It started as a mobile-notary scheduling tool and grew into a digital mortgage-closing platform valued at about $2B. He led it as CEO for a decade, then handed the CEO role to Michael Sachdev in Sept 2023 and stayed on full-time as executive chairman, focused on product direction and customers.
interesting_fact: He was a mortgage-industry veteran of roughly 20 years who worked as a notary signing agent himself. That front-line experience led to a nationwide notary signing service and eventually Snapdocs.
deep_cut_fact: Asked for the best advice he ever received, he said: 'There's tremendous power in being a great listener... hyper-effective leaders continuously hone this skill.'

public_contacts.value: Sam Garcia, Strategic Vantage Marketing & PR - samgarcia@strategicvantage.com

notes: Aggregator sites say his earlier notary company was NotaryLink, founded at age 21; I could not confirm this from a primary source. Contacts come from a Sept 2023 release.

name: Ziv Paz
current_role: Co-founder (non-operational) of Melio (former COO); current venture not verified
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Melio, a B2B payments platform for small businesses, in 2018 with Matan Bar and Ilan Atias. As COO and the company's number two he led operations and go-to-market. He gave up his operational role in 2021. Xero agreed in 2025 to buy Melio for up to $3B, and CTech reported that each co-founder holds about 9%.
interesting_fact: He was the only Melio founder without a technology background. He studied law and accounting after long service in the IDF naval commando unit Shayetet 13.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 2.5 years as a VP at FIMI Opportunity Funds and was on track to run a portfolio company and return as a partner. He left instead to start Melio with Matan Bar, his childhood school friend from Haifa.
notes: Left his operational role at Melio in 2021 (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3923561,00.html). Melio is now part of Xero. An aggregator says he started a new company in 2024; I could not verify this. No published contact found; LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Malte Horeyseck
current_role: Co-founder, SellerX (former co-CEO); current operating role unclear
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded SellerX, a Berlin-based Amazon-brand aggregator, with Harvard Business School friend Philipp Triebel in summer 2020. It raised a then-record €100M seed round and reached a $1B valuation. Press reports say both founders stepped down as co-CEOs in mid-2024. Since then SellerX has gone through a recapitalisation and CEO changes.
interesting_fact: After HBS he moved to Brazil and, in SellerX's words, 'built Latin America's leading ecommerce platform from scratch'; Crunchbase lists him as a Dafiti co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: He and Philipp Triebel met at HBS in Boston, then lived on opposite sides of the world (Brazil and London) and kept discussing a joint business for years before founding SellerX in summer 2020.
notes: Search results said he and Triebel stepped down as co-CEOs in June 2024, citing Sifted (https://sifted.eu/articles/sellerx-ceos-depart-share-sale-news), but I could not open that article. The company has been under financial strain since. Use a neutral approach, and LinkedIn is likely the best route. He was interviewed on the Tech.eu podcast: https://podcast.tech.eu/episodes/malte-horeyseck-co-founder-of-sellerx-interview-special

name: Hari Ravichandran
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aura (digital safety; ASX: AXQ after the 2026 Qoria merger)
profile: Indian-born American serial founder. He started BizLand, which grew into Endurance International Group (Bluehost, HostGator), and ran it until 2017. He has been CEO of Aura, a consumer identity-theft and online-safety company, since 2019. In 2026 Aura completed its acquisition of Australia's Qoria, creating a group with more than $300M ARR that trades on the ASX as AXQ.
interesting_fact: He started BizLand with most of his $8,000 savings. After the dot-com crash he cut staff to 14 and made customers pay subscriptions; only about 2% converted, yet the company broke even the next year on $2M revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Instead of spending on marketing, Endurance grew by buying small hosting firms with 2,000-5,000 customers each, often with seller financing. His lesson from the crash: 'If you don't focus on profitability, things can go bad.'
notes: Aura's bio says he has an MBA from Wharton, a computer engineering degree from Mississippi State and studied electrical engineering at Stanford. He founded the Ravichandran Foundation (Boston area and India; source: latinpost). Aura is now ASX-listed, so ASX investor-relations channels apply.

name: Li Xuelin
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Hefu Laomian (和府捞面) noodle restaurant chain
profile: Li Xuelin (李学林) founded Hefu Laomian in 2012. The premium Chinese noodle chain is known for its 'noodles in a study room' store concept and central-kitchen supply chain. It raised more than RMB1.6B in six rounds from 2016 to 2022 and reached roughly $1B valuation. Since late 2023 it has pursued expansion through franchising/joint operation, lower-tier cities and overseas markets.
interesting_fact: Before restaurants he ran a leading mobile-phone retailer in Jiangsu. He says he has 'led troops' for over 20 years across phone retail and restaurant chains.
deep_cut_fact: He has said China's restaurant industry has produced no giants 'not because of too few categories or projects, but because of missing systems and core capabilities', which is why Hefu built its own supply chain.
notes: Based in mainland China and media-light. Chinese-language outreach through Hefu Laomian corporate channels is likely the best route. I found no published contact email.

name: Tobias Schreyer
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (former Chief Commercial Officer); not on PPRO's current leadership page
profile: German payments entrepreneur who co-founded PPRO, the London-based local-payments infrastructure provider, with Philipp Nieland in 2006. PPRO was later valued at about $1B. As CCO he helped secure PPRO's UK FCA e-money licence in 2012 and launch its VIABUY prepaid card. As an undergraduate he started a Munich internet service provider.
interesting_fact: His interest in payments started in childhood: he collected prepaid calling cards and traded them at exchanges.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 PYMNTS interview he said he commuted 50 miles to work by bike, using the ride to plan his day. He also said: 'you need to have failed at some point in your career; otherwise you don't know the essentials.'
notes: He is not listed on PPRO's current leadership page (CEO is Motie Bring), so his current role is unverified. Low public profile; LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Deng Xianliang
current_role: (If same person) Founder & CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments)
profile: XTransfer's founder and CEO is Bill Deng (邓国标, Deng Guobiao), who launched it in May 2017 with five former Ant Group colleagues as a 'B2B Alipay' for Chinese SME exporters. He previously spent more than a decade in payments at Visa and Ant Financial. Fortune reported in 2026 that XTransfer serves over 800,000 businesses and processes over $12B a month.
interesting_fact: Fortune reported in 2026 that XTransfer handles more than 2% of China's exports. 'Global South' countries now make up 70% of its payments, while the US share fell from 22% to 9%.
deep_cut_fact: Deng says seven years at Alipay showed him that consumer payment rails were mature while B2B cross-border payments were still badly served. Former colleagues leaving to found companies such as Didi pushed him to start his own.
notes: Name mismatch: Hurun lists 'Deng Xianliang', but every source I found names XTransfer's founder and CEO as Bill Deng / 邓国标 (Deng Guobiao). Confirm this is the same person before outreach. He speaks often at fintech conferences such as Money20/20 and the Singapore FinTech Festival.
